SCENARIO: User.from_omniauth on an EXISTING user (matching email) must NOT modify the 4 attribution columns (creation-time-only). Env: cleanup + seed default-user-and-org.json, then test_frr (RAILS_ENV=test) script /tmp/l3_r2_a2_existing_user_not_modified.rb via login-shell+cd form. Set ActiveJob queue_adapter=:test in-script so the inline UserSetupJob/NotifyUserJob (real Slack under test.rb:64 :inline) did not fire; auth had nil first/last name so update_marketing_contact guard stayed false. Code under test app/models/user.rb:379-410 assigns the 4 utm cols ONLY inside the where(email:).first_or_create block (creation), then unconditionally user.update(first_name:,last_name:) only.

CASE A (existing user WITH distinct original values): seeded User id=39368 utm_source="original_src" utm_campaign="original_camp" utm_data={"utm_medium"=>"original"} internal_ref="original_ref". Called User.from_omniauth(auth:same email, created_via:'created_via_signup', utm_source/utm_campaign/internal_ref:'ShouldNotStick', utm_data:{'utm_medium'=>'ShouldNotStick'}). RESULT: User.count 2->2 (found, not created); returned.id=39368==seeded.id; RELOADED id=39368 utm_source="original_src" utm_campaign="original_camp" utm_data={"utm_medium"=>"original"} internal_ref="original_ref" — all four UNCHANGED, none became 'ShouldNotStick'.

CASE B (existing user with ALL-NIL utm): seeded User id=39369 utm_source=nil utm_campaign=nil utm_data=nil internal_ref=nil. Same from_omniauth call with all 'ShouldNotStick'. RESULT: User.count 3->3 (found, not created); returned.id=39369==seeded.id; RELOADED id=39369 utm_source=nil utm_campaign=nil utm_data=nil internal_ref=nil — all four still nil (utm_data nil, NOT {}), none stuck.

VERDICT: PASS. Existing users are never modified on later login/from_omniauth; the four attribution columns are write-once at row creation. No findings.
